# Moneyya Sutta (Iti 67 (It 3.18 PTS It 56))

**ID:** Iti 67 (It 3.18 PTS It 56)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Moneyya Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Moneyya Sutta* ("Sagacity", *Iti* 67; PTS It 56) is a short discourse in the third section (*Tikanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka*. The sutta outlines three forms of sagacity (*moneyya*): bodily (*kāya-moneyya*), verbal (*vacī-moneyya*), and mental (*mano-moneyya*) [Moore 1908]. The concluding verses state that an ascetic who is restrained and pure in body, speech, and mind, and endowed with the silence or sagacity of a sage (*muni-moneyya*), is rightly said to have cleansed away all evil [Moore 1908].

In early historical scholarship on King Aśoka's Bhabru (Calcutta-Bairat) rock edict, Charles Eliot noted that the tract designated by the emperor as *Moneyasute* was identified by some scholars with this *Itivuttaka* discourse [Eliot 1921].

 DharmaNexus matches corroborate this parallel, showing extensive shared text with the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3.122) as well as substantial structural and phrasing overlap with adjacent *Itivuttaka* suttas—including *Soceyya Sutta* (Iti 66), *Duccarita Sutta* (Iti 64), *Cakkhu Sutta* (Iti 61), *Indriya Sutta* (Iti 62), and *Sucarita Sutta* (Iti 65)—and the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects text reuse between this sutta and the Tibetan version of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090) [DharmaNexus].
